#### 1. epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to plakophilin deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.436)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6809371, Reactome:R-HSA-6805567)

**Proposed mechanism:** KRT6C (HGNC:6476) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial cell cytoskeleton organization and stability (GO:0030030); PKP1 (HGNC:9024) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial cell cytoskeleton organization and stability (GO:0030030); Epithelial cell cytoskeleton organization and stability (GO:0030030) —LEADS_TO→ Blistering skin fragility (HP:0007374); Epithelial cell cytoskeleton organization and stability (GO:0030030) —LEADS_TO→ Skin fragility (HP:0007374). Loss-of-function mutations in KRT6C (disease A) and PKP1 (disease B) both disrupt the organization and stability of the epithelial cell cytoskeleton, leading to compromised skin integrity and blistering.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in KRT6C or PKP1 with a minor allele frequency >0.1% in gnomAD would falsify their role as causal genes in these rare diseases. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in KRT6C or PKP1 with high frequency in gnomAD.)_

#### 2. arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia 9  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.381)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6809371, Reactome:R-HSA-6805567)

**Proposed mechanism:** PKP2 (HGNC:9003) —DISRUPTS→ Desmosomal adhesion (GO:0034773); KRT6C (HGNC:6476) —DISRUPTS→ Desmosomal adhesion (GO:0034773); Desmosomal adhesion (GO:0034773) —LEADS_TO→ Arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia (HP:0011676); Desmosomal adhesion (GO:0034773) —LEADS_TO→ Unspecified phenotype (MONDO:0014327). Loss-of-function mutations in PKP2 disrupt desmosomal adhesion, leading to arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia. While KRT6C is also implicated in the unnamed disease (MONDO:0014327), it is proposed that this disease also results from a disruption of desmosomal adhesion, potentially through interaction with PKP2 or independent disruption of the same pathway.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic analysis reveals that mutations in PKP2 do not lead to loss-of-function in both diseases, or if the two diseases are demonstrably linked to entirely separate cellular pathways with no overlap in protein complexes or downstream effects, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: The presence of common variants (>1% allele frequency) in PKP2 in the gnomAD database that are not associated with either disease would also challenge the causal role of PKP2 in these specific conditions.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this shared mechanism could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia and the unnamed disease, potentially by stabilizing desmosomal junctions or mitigating downstream effects of their disruption.
